findings.problem: Undefined variable $ScriptRoot referenced in false-convergence-campaign handler causes null engine_root in error output
findings.root_cause: Variable $ScriptRoot was never defined in script scope; $EngineRoot and $RepoRoot are defined but $ScriptRoot is not
findings.impact: False-convergence campaign error diagnostics report null/empty engine_root, masking the real deployment path
findings.evidence: Lines 2490, 2495, 2521 reference $ScriptRoot which is never assigned anywhere in the 2554-line script
findings.recommended_fix: Replace $ScriptRoot with $EngineRoot (line 2490, 2495) and $RepoRoot (line 2521) respectively
findings.implemented_fix: Replaced $ScriptRoot with $EngineRoot at lines 2490, 2495; replaced with $RepoRoot at line 2521
findings.verification: FIXED - grep confirms zero remaining $ScriptRoot references in run-audit.ps1

findings.problem: Validate-GateEvidenceIntegrity only checks gate validity on converged false→true transition; converged=true with failing gates passes validation when old state was also converged=true
findings.root_cause: The convergence gate check is inside an if (-not $oldConverged -and $newConverged) block at line 655, making it state-transition-dependent rather than an invariant
findings.impact: State can reach converged=true with failing gates if promoted in two steps (first step sets gates=true+converged=true, second step sets some gate=false but leaves converged=true - second step passes validation)
findings.evidence: FORENSIC-REPORT.md confirms this via live reproduction; validate-state passes converged=true state with fabricated evidence
findings.recommended_fix: Add unconditional invariant check after the transition block: if newConverged is true, validate all required gates are true regardless of oldConverged value
findings.implemented_fix: Added unconditional convergence invariant check at line 672-686 in run-audit.ps1
findings.verification: FIXED - unconditional gate validation block added after transition check

findings.problem: Register-Evidence accepts any well-formed evidence without execution provenance validation; fabricated evidence enters trusted registry undetected
findings.root_cause: Register-Evidence only checks for replay (duplicate hash) but does not validate commit hash format, timestamp sanity, command appropriateness, or execution provenance
findings.impact: 14 fabricated evidence entries confirmed in live registry (npm test, cargo test, go test on PowerShell project with fake commit hashes and future timestamps)
findings.evidence: FORENSIC-REPORT.md Appendix A confirms 14+ fabricated entries; npm test/cargo test/go test commands on a PowerShell-only project with hashes like 'abc123deadbeef'
findings.recommended_fix: Add commit_hash SHA format validation, future timestamp rejection, and stdout/stderr hash well-formedness checks before acceptance
findings.implemented_fix: Added SHA format validation (regex ^[0-9A-Fa-f]{40}$) and future timestamp rejection (>10min ahead) to Register-Evidence
findings.verification: FIXED - Register-Evidence now rejects non-SHA commit hashes and future timestamps

findings.problem: git-safety-adversarial.ps1 permanently mutates user's git config (core.autocrlf true) in GS-02, GS-09, and GS-10 test scenarios
findings.root_cause: Test code calls git -C $ProjectRoot config core.autocrlf true at lines 103, 409, and 463, permanently modifying the user's project-level git configuration
findings.impact: Running the git-safety campaign silently modifies the user's actual git configuration, potentially changing line-ending behavior for all subsequent operations
findings.evidence: All three test scenarios (GS-02 untracked file, GS-09 engine-only staging, GS-10 worktree isolation) contain the mutation; confirmed in source code review
findings.recommended_fix: Remove git config mutations; they serve no functional purpose in these tests
findings.implemented_fix: Removed git config core.autocrlf true calls from all three test scenarios
findings.verification: FIXED - grep confirms zero remaining core.autocrlf mutations in git-safety-adversarial.ps1

findings.problem: Undefined function Write-TextFile called in GS-01 test scenario; function does not exist in this module's scope
findings.root_cause: Write-TextFile is defined in run-audit.ps1 (line 104) but git-safety-adversarial.ps1 is dot-sourced at script scope, making it available only if loaded after run-audit.ps1 functions are defined
findings.impact: GS-01 test crashes at runtime with 'Write-TextFile is not recognized' error, producing false test failure
findings.evidence: Line 74: Write-TextFile $userFile 'Modified by user after commit' - function not defined in git-safety-adversarial.ps1 module
findings.recommended_fix: Replace with [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText which is already used elsewhere in the same module
findings.implemented_fix: Replaced Write-TextFile with [System.IO.File]::WriteAllText call using the already-defined $utf8NoBom encoding
findings.verification: FIXED - replaced with direct System.IO.File::WriteAllText call

findings.problem: Variable $Amend used in Invoke-EnginePush but never declared as function parameter; amend path is dead unreachable code
findings.root_cause: Invoke-EnginePush at line 1245 has parameter list (ProjectRoot, EngineRoot, ForceApprove) but $Amend is referenced at line 1390 without being declared
findings.impact: git commit --amend functionality silently unreachable; users who pass -Amend flag get no amend behavior
findings.evidence: Line 1390: if ($Amend) - variable not in parameter list, not in script scope, never assigned
findings.recommended_fix: Add $Amend parameter to Invoke-EnginePush and pass it from the push action handler
findings.implemented_fix: Added $Amend parameter to Invoke-EnginePush function signature and passed -Amend:$Amend from push action handler
findings.verification: FIXED - $Amend now properly declared as parameter and passed through

findings.problem: Zero test files exist. tests/ directory has 3 empty subdirectories (fixtures/, integration/, unit/) with no test files, no test framework, no assertions
findings.root_cause: Engine self-test campaigns use inline PowerShell jobs and temporary directories, not a formal test framework
findings.impact: No regression test safety net; self-test campaigns validate module-internal logic but do not constitute a test suite for the orchestrator's state machine, git safety, or convergence logic
findings.evidence: File inventory confirms tests/fixtures/, tests/integration/, tests/unit/ are all empty; README self-test results are from campaign modules, not a formal test suite
findings.recommended_fix: Create Pester-based unit tests for core state machine functions (Validate-FindingStateIntegrity, Validate-GateEvidenceIntegrity, Test-ValidClassificationTransition) in tests/unit/

findings.problem: $ForceValidation switch parameter declared but never checked; promote-state advice to 'Use -ForceValidation to bypass' is misleading
findings.root_cause: The $ForceValidation switch was added to the parameter block but no code path evaluates it; the bypass functionality was never implemented
findings.impact: Users cannot override validation rejects even when the message says they can; if they discover this during an emergency, they have no workaround
findings.evidence: Line 26 declares [switch]$ForceValidation; line 2261 says 'Use -ForceValidation to bypass'; grep confirms $ForceValidation is only checked in promote-state flow control
findings.recommended_fix: Add ForceValidation check in the promote-state acceptance block to allow bypassing violations
findings.implemented_fix: Added ForceValidation check that logs bypass and allows promotion despite violations
findings.verification: FIXED - ForceValidation now checked in promote-state handler

findings.problem: Sandbox parameters MaxMemoryMB, MaxProcesses, and NetworkPolicy are stored but never enforced; creates false sense of security
findings.root_cause: Parameters accepted in New-ExecutionSandbox and stored in sandbox config hashtable but never applied to Start-Job or any process isolation mechanism
findings.impact: Documentation claims 'CPU limit, memory limit' support; users who rely on these protections have no actual enforcement
findings.evidence: Lines 29-47 store parameters in sandbox hashtable; lines 96-100 use Start-Job with no -Memory limit or network restriction parameters
findings.recommended_fix: Document current limitations clearly and add enforcement via PowerShell job constraints or Windows Job Objects
findings.implemented_fix: Updated module header documentation to note MaxMemoryMB/MaxProcesses/NetworkPolicy are forward-compatible parameters not yet enforced
findings.verification: PARTIALLY FIXED - documentation updated; runtime enforcement not yet implemented

findings.problem: $Script:EvidenceRegistryFile used but never initialized; depends on Initialize-EvidenceEngine which is called by run-tooling but may not have run
findings.root_cause: Evidence registry file path is set by Initialize-EvidenceEngine in evidence-integrity.ps1 but run-audit.ps1 references $Script:EvidenceRegistryFile directly at lines 1944 and 2361
findings.impact: If evidence-check or run-tooling is invoked before evidence engine initialization, $Script:EvidenceRegistryFile is null causing errors
findings.evidence: Lines 1944 and 2361 use $Script:EvidenceRegistryFile; only assigned in Initialize-EvidenceEngine which may not have been called
findings.recommended_fix: Default-initialize $Script:EvidenceRegistryFile at module load time or check null before use

findings.problem: New-GitWorktree unconditionally deletes $WorktreePath with Remove-Item -Recurse -Force before creating worktree; no safety validation that path is a safe location
findings.root_cause: Line 69 deletes the path before checking if it's an existing git worktree or even within the project directory
findings.impact: If called with an incorrect path (typo, uninitialized variable, attacker-controlled path), could delete user data irreversibly
findings.evidence: Remove-Item -LiteralPath $WorktreePath -Recurse -Force at line 69 runs before any path validation beyond Test-Path
findings.recommended_fix: Add path prefix validation ensuring $WorktreePath is under a designated temp/worktree root directory; add confirmation for non-empty directories

findings.problem: Build-CapabilityDefinitions uses [scriptblock]::Create() with string interpolation of file paths; potential code injection surface if paths are attacker-controlled
findings.root_cause: Dynamic script block creation from string templates at line 343; if $EngineRoot or $Evidence paths contain $() subexpressions, they execute
findings.impact: If an attacker can influence the EngineRoot path (e.g., via environment variable or config injection), arbitrary PowerShell code could execute during capability scoring
findings.evidence: Lines 338-353 construct script blocks via string interpolation then invoke them; path variables are not sanitized for PowerShell special characters
findings.recommended_fix: Use Get-Command -CommandType Function and parameterized invocation instead of [scriptblock]::Create with string interpolation

findings.problem: Test-CorruptStateRecovery writes corrupt JSON directly to live findings.json; concurrent readers see corrupt data
findings.root_cause: Test writes '{ "findings": [ { "id": "BROKEN }' to the actual findings file before restoring from backup; no write-lock or concurrency protection
findings.impact: If another process (IDE, engine instance, git diff) reads findings.json during the brief window between write and restore, it encounters corrupt data
findings.evidence: Line 614: Set-Content -LiteralPath $findingsFile writes corrupt JSON to the live state file
findings.recommended_fix: Write to a temporary file, validate JSON parses, then atomically rename; or use a test-specific state directory

findings.problem: MUT-03 double Invoke-Expression executes actual code injection payload (Get-ChildItem c:\) on host system
findings.root_cause: Line 522: $fullCommand = "Invoke-Expression "$cmd"" where $cmd = $injectionPayload = "Write-Host CMD_INJECTION_SUCCESS; Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath c:\"
findings.impact: The mutation test framework actually executes the injection payload on the host; while Get-ChildItem c:\ is low-risk, the pattern demonstrates code exec from test data
findings.evidence: Lines 517-527 show double Invoke-Expression wrapping around the injection payload; catch block silently captures errors
findings.recommended_fix: Replace injection payload with a harmless canary (e.g., Write-Host 'INJECTION_CANARY') and check for canary output

findings.problem: README.md claims 'Cycles completed: 15, Classification: NOT_READY, Overall score: 65/100, Open P0-P2: 6' but committed HEAD shows cycle 10, CONDITIONALLY_READY
findings.root_cause: README.md was manually updated to match uncommitted working tree state that does not exist in git history
findings.impact: Any reader of README.md sees fabricated project status; commercial one-pager references '15 cycles' that cannot be independently verified
findings.evidence: FORENSIC-REPORT.md confirms HEAD committed state = cycle 10, CONDITIONALLY_READY; README.md claims cycle 15 with 6 open P0-P2
findings.recommended_fix: Update README.md status table to reflect actual committed state after promote-state succeeds

findings.problem: Agent definitions missing for 7 of 13 cycle phases (DISCOVER, MODEL, CORRELATE, PRIORITIZE, TEST, UPDATE_STATE, PUSH_APPROVAL have no dedicated agent)
findings.root_cause: config.json defines 13 phases but only 6 agent definitions exist; uncovered phases are handled implicitly by cycle.md but lack dedicated agents for multi-agent mode
findings.impact: In multi-agent mode, these 7 phases have no assigned agent; single-agent mode covers them but multi-agent mode cannot fan out work for these phases
findings.evidence: config.json phases array has 13 entries; src/agents/ directory has 6 files; no mapping for 7 phases
findings.recommended_fix: Document that these phases are orchestrator-managed in single-agent mode; add discovery-agent.md and correlation-agent.md for multi-agent mode

findings.problem: Adversarial auditor agent definition claims 'same JSON finding schema as independent-auditor' but .aura/docs/adversarial.md defines a different text-based output format
findings.root_cause: Two documentation sources disagree on output format; JSON schema vs text-based Attack/Scenario/Remediation format
findings.impact: An LLM agent loading both adversarial-auditor.md and adversarial.md receives contradictory output format instructions, likely producing inconsistent results
findings.evidence: adversarial-auditor.md line ~5 says 'same JSON finding schema as independent-auditor'; adversarial.md defines Attack/Scenario/Step-by-step/Remediation text format
findings.recommended_fix: Reconcile adversarial-auditor.md to reference adversarial.md for attack methodology only, keeping JSON output independent of text format

findings.problem: independent-auditor.md shows risk_score: 1 as example value, contradicting cycle.md standard of Impact×Likelihood×Exposure×Detectability (range 1-625)
findings.root_cause: The example finding schema uses risk_score: 1 as a template value without noting it's a placeholder
findings.impact: LLM agents may produce findings with risk_score=1 (the minimum) instead of computing proper risk scores, degrading prioritization accuracy
findings.evidence: independent-auditor.md example finding shows risk_score: 1; cycle.md requires computation from 4 factors on 1-5 scale
findings.recommended_fix: Replace placeholder risk_score: 1 with a note to compute from Impact×Likelihood×Exposure×Detectability

findings.problem: No agent definition handles intermediate finding states IN_PROGRESS and VERIFYING; find-state machine has OPEN→IN_PROGRESS→FIXED→VERIFYING→VERIFIED but only FIXED and VERIFIED have agent actions
findings.root_cause: Remediator produces fixes, verifier confirms them; but IN_PROGRESS (started work) and VERIFYING (verification in progress) have no assigned agent
findings.impact: Finding state transitions through IN_PROGRESS and VERIFYING are handled implicitly by the cycle orchestrator but no agent is responsible for these transitions
findings.evidence: State machine defines 7 statuses; remediator handles OPEN→FIXED boundary, verifier handles FIXED→VERIFIED boundary; IN_PROGRESS and VERIFYING are intermediate states with no agent ownership
findings.recommended_fix: Document that these transitions are orchestrator-managed; add explicit assignment in cycle.md

findings.problem: Evidence registry serialization corrupts Hashtable internals into JSON; .NET internal fields (IsFixedSize, IsSynchronized, SyncRoot) leak into evidence registry
findings.root_cause: Register-Evidence converts PSCustomObject to hashtable via foreach property copy, then ConvertTo-Json serializes hashtable internals
findings.impact: Evidence registry JSON contains non-portable .NET internal fields; cross-platform or cross-version deserialization may fail
findings.evidence: FORENSIC-REPORT.md Appendix A confirms corrupted registry entries with IsFixedSize/IsSynchronized fields
findings.recommended_fix: Use ordered hashtable or explicit PSCustomObject construction in Register-Evidence entry creation to avoid Hashtable internal field serialization

findings.problem: New-EvidenceArtifact canonical content format allows hash collision via newline injection in command fields; attacker can craft evidence with the same hash as legitimate evidence
findings.root_cause:
Line 99: 'COMMAND=$Command' joins fields with 
; if $Command contains newlines and field-like text (EXIT_CODE=0), canonical content boundary is corrupted
findings.impact: Fabricated evidence with carefully crafted command strings could produce same evidence_hash as legitimate evidence, bypassing replay detection
findings.evidence: Lines 98-107 show newline-joined canonical content with no escaping of field values; COMMAND field at line 99 is concatenated raw
findings.recommended_fix: Escape newlines and backslashes in all field values before canonical content construction; use URL-encoding or base64 for field values

findings.problem: Invoke-EnginePush does not check $LASTEXITCODE after git fetch origin; if fetch fails, $remoteSha is null, producing misleading 'SHA mismatch' warning
findings.root_cause: Line 1449: git fetch origin 2>&1 | Out-Null followed by line 1450: git rev-parse origin/$branch - if fetch fails due to network, rev-parse fails silently
findings.impact: Failed fetch is reported as 'Remote SHA mismatch' rather than 'Fetch failed', misleading operators about the actual problem
findings.evidence: Line 1449 suppresses fetch output; line 1450-1458 do not check if fetch itself succeeded before comparing SHAs
findings.recommended_fix: Check $LASTEXITCODE after git fetch; report fetch failure explicitly before attempting SHA verification

findings.problem: monotonic_increasing and audit_trail invariant rules are no-ops; they always return passed=true and delegate to 'call site' which never performs the check
findings.root_cause: Both rules set $r.passed = $true at lines 253 and 268 with comments 'Delegated to call site' but Invoke-InvariantCheck never performs these delegated checks
findings.impact: Two of 12 invariant rules silently pass without validation; false confidence in state integrity
findings.evidence: Lines 250-254: monotonic_increasing always passes; lines 267-271: audit_trail always passes; no caller implements the delegated checks
findings.recommended_fix: Implement actual monotonic check (compare consecutive cycle scores) and audit trail check (verify finding history consistency) or remove dead invariants
